notes: Sample sla_policies.json - the service level objectives the collected metrics are graded against. Copy to sla_policies.json and edit.

An SLO here is a claim you are prepared to be held to, computed from metric history rather than from a separate probe. That is the whole point: the numbers on the report and the numbers behind the objective come from the same measurements.

'metric_codes' names the metrics that make up the indicator; 'aggregation' says how they combine, and 'good_statuses' says which recorded outcomes count as success. Everything else is derived from those.

'window_hours' is the rolling window. 'objective_percent' is the target. 'at_risk_budget_percent' is how much of the remaining error budget triggers a warning before the objective is actually missed - reporting only the breach is reporting it too late.
'minimum_sample_count' refuses to state a verdict on too little data. Without it, one successful sample in a fresh window reads as 100%, which is the most confident wrong answer the system can give.

'expected_collection_interval_seconds' and 'freshness_threshold_seconds' turn 'we stopped measuring' into a visible outcome rather than a silent gap. 'missing_data_policy': 'unknown' records the gap as unknown instead of quietly counting it as success.
'required' false marks an objective as tracked but not committed to - useful while an objective is being calibrated against a few weeks of real data.

'notification.reminder_after_seconds' is the ceiling on re-stating a finding that has not moved. The hourly run only messages when state changes; this stops a standing problem being silently forgotten without turning the channel back into noise.

sla_policies.name: Multi-engine availability
sla_policies.description: Every monitored instance and database reports a healthy status across the last 24 hours.

sla_policies.name: Backup freshness
sla_policies.description: Every database required to be backed up has a backup inside its policy window.
sla_policies._note: A week-long window, because the thing being measured is a daily-or-slower event. The per-database thresholds themselves are in backup_policy.json - this objective grades how often those were met.

sla_policies.name: Monitoring coverage
sla_policies.description: The monitoring itself kept running: every enabled target produced samples at the expected rate.
sla_policies._note: The objective that watches the watcher. Without it, an estate that silently stopped being collected from scores perfectly on every other objective.

sla_policies.name: PostgreSQL replication health
sla_policies.description: Standbys stayed connected and replication slots stayed active.
sla_policies._note: 'required': false while the objective is being calibrated. Promote it once a few weeks of real data show what this estate normally looks like.

sla_policies.name: PostgreSQL transaction ID safety
sla_policies.description: No database approached transaction ID wraparound.
sla_policies._note: One hundred percent, deliberately. Some objectives have no acceptable failure rate, and this is one of them: the failure mode is the cluster refusing to accept writes.
